easy.def: A word used to show two things at the same time.
examples: I sang as I walked.
She smiled as she hugged him.
The sun set as we ate.

more.def: A word used to show that two things happen at the same time, or that one thing is the reason for another.
examples: The audience clapped as the dancers took a bow.
As it was raining, we had the party indoors.
He hummed a tune as he washed the dishes.

easy.def: A word used to show what someone or something is or does.
examples: She works as a nurse.
I used a box as a chair.
He dressed as a pirate.

more.def: A word used to show the job, role, or purpose of someone or something.
examples: My aunt works as a firefighter in our town.
We used a blanket as a tent in the living room.
The famous dog served as a mascot for the team.

easy.def: Feeling bad because you did something wrong.
examples: I felt ashamed of my lie.
He was ashamed of what he said.
She looked ashamed.

more.def: Feeling sorry and a little embarrassed about something you did.
examples: He was ashamed that he had broken the window.
She felt ashamed of how she shouted at her friend.
Do not be ashamed to ask for help when you need it.

easy.def: The gray powder that is left after something burns.
examples: The fire left ashes.
We cleaned out the ashes.
The ashes are gray.

more.def: The soft gray powder that remains after something has burned.
examples: The campfire left a pile of ashes.
We swept the ashes out of the fireplace.
The ashes were still warm.

easy.def: On or to the land from the sea.
examples: The boat came ashore.
We swam ashore.
The sailors went ashore.

more.def: To or onto the land from the water.
examples: The boat came ashore at dawn.
Waves carried the driftwood ashore.
The sailors went ashore for supplies.
Please move aside.
I put the book aside.
She stepped aside.

more.def: To one side, or out of the way.
examples: He stepped aside to let the others pass.
Set your work aside and come to dinner.
She put some money aside for a new bike.

easy.def: To say something so someone will answer.
examples: I ask my teacher.
She asked a question.
Ask Dad for help.

more.def: To put a question to someone, or to request something from someone.
examples: I asked the librarian where the animal books are.
He asked his grandmother to tell the story again.
May I ask you a question about the experiment?
The baby is asleep.
The cat is asleep.
I fell asleep in the car.

more.def: In a state of sleep; not awake.
examples: The baby fell asleep in the car.
The whole house was asleep by midnight.
My legs fell asleep after I sat for a long time.
That is one aspect of the problem.
The aspect is new.
Each aspect is important.

more.def: One part or feature of something.
examples: One aspect of the story I liked was the setting.
The best aspect of the trip was the beach.
Look at every aspect of the plan.
I assemble the toy.
They assembled the bike.
We assemble the model.

more.def: To put the parts of something together, or to gather people together.
examples: Dad assembled the bike from the box.
We assembled the model airplane.
The students assembled in the gym.

easy.def: To give someone a job to do.
examples: The teacher assigned a project.
She assigned me a chore.
Mom assigns the jobs.

more.def: To give someone a job or task to do.
examples: The teacher assigned a book to read.
She assigned each child a job.
Mom assigned me to feed the dog.

easy.def: Work that a teacher tells you to do.
examples: Our assignment is to read a book.
The assignment is due tomorrow.
I finished my assignment.

more.def: A piece of work that someone gives you to do.
examples: Our assignment is to write a story about a pet.
The science assignment is due on Friday.
I finished the assignment before dinner.
I assist my teacher.
She assisted the nurse.
He assisted with the cooking.
I assisted the teacher by handing out papers.
The nurse assisted the doctor.
He assisted the old woman across the street.
I need assistance.
She asked for assistance.
The nurse gave assistance.

more.def: Help or support that someone gives you.
examples: I need assistance with my homework.
The firefighters came to give assistance.
He asked for assistance with the heavy box.
The teacher has an assistant.
I am his assistant.
The assistant carried the box.

more.def: A person who helps someone do a job.
examples: The teacher's assistant passed out papers.
The chef's assistant chopped the carrots.
The doctor's assistant took my temperature.

easy.def: To connect things in your mind.
examples: I associate summer with swimming.
She associates that song with her grandmother.
We associate red with stop.

more.def: To connect one thing to another in your mind.
examples: I associate the smell of bread with my grandma.
Many people associate the color red with danger.
She associates the song with her grandfather.

easy.def: A group of people with a shared purpose.
examples: I joined an association.
The association meets monthly.
The sports association planned a game.

more.def: An organization of people who have the same job or interest.
examples: My parents joined the neighborhood association.
The soccer association plans the games.
The nurses' association met on Friday.

easy.def: To think something is true without checking.
examples: I assume you are hungry.
She assumed it was Monday.
We assume it will rain.

more.def: To think that something is true without knowing for sure.
examples: I assumed the store was open, but it was closed.
Do not assume everyone likes spicy food.
She assumed the bus was late.

easy.def: A person who goes into space.
examples: The astronaut waved from the rocket.
I want to be an astronaut one day.
The astronaut floats in space.

more.def: A person trained to travel and work in space.
examples: The astronaut lived on the space station for six months.
An astronaut wears a special suit to stay safe outside the ship.
The astronauts fixed the telescope while circling the Earth.
